requirements.requirement: Run a containerized web application on node1 as the unprivileged account appsvc
requirements.summary: cmd-c44b686d98f7460a shows a rootless Podman Quadlet unit (webapp.service) executed via `sudo -u appsvc` with XDG_RUNTIME_DIR set to appsvc's runtime dir, running the httpd:alpine image under appsvc's user systemd instance (user@1000.service), confirmed active with httpd worker processes. appsvc was created as a normal (uid 1000) unprivileged user with subuid/subgid ranges (cmd-5a89da8503614918).

cmd-c44b686d98f7460a shows the Quadlet unit publishing 8080:80 via pasta, `ss -tlnp` listing a listener on *:8080, and a local curl to NODE_IP:8080 returning HTTP 200. The global after_executor listening-sockets snapshot independently confirms the new *:8080 listener owned by the pasta process, and cmd-48f94b3b6e53420e reconfirms HTTP 200 after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Service starts at boot while the appsvc account has no active login session
requirements.summary: Lingering was enabled for appsvc (cmd-5a89da8503614918, loginctl show-user Linger=yes). Pre-reboot, cmd-ef0c45bcb3074ae5 captured a healthy baseline (webapp.service/HTTP 200 established just prior, empty loginctl list-sessions, boot_id 4a743885...) and cmd-45377ebaa2e24524 issued and acknowledged `systemctl reboot`. Post-reboot, cmd-352fa72b27ce42ba shows a different boot_id (a0b068f5...) and fresh uptime, and cmd-48f94b3b6e53420e shows webapp.service and user@1000.service active since the new boot time, the 8080 listener present, HTTP 200, and loginctl list-sessions still empty (only lingering state) — directly demonstrating boot-time autostart without an active session across a real, bounded disruption.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task — a containerized web app run as the unprivileged appsvc account, serving on port 8080, and starting at boot without an active login session — are directly satisfied with evidence spanning a real pre-reboot baseline, an acknowledged reboot, a changed boot identity, and full post-reboot recovery of the service, listener, and HTTP endpoint while appsvc remained session-less (lingering only). This also fulfills the provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol for the sole managed node, node1, cross-checked consistently against the fixed before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity and listening-socket snapshots. Hygiene is good; the only findings are two small leftover log files in /tmp with no functional or security impact.
limitations: Only a single reboot cycle was captured; longer-term persistence across multiple reboots was not tested.
Two /tmp log files (dnf-podman.log, pull.log) remain as minor uncleaned residue but do not affect functionality or security.

operational_hygiene.summary: Chronological review of executor commands shows each state-changing action mapped to a clear purpose: installing podman, creating appsvc, enabling linger, opening the firewall port, pulling the image, writing the Quadlet unit, and starting the service all directly build the required deployment; the reboot commands were the necessary, task-relevant boot-behavior verification. The two nonzero-return commands (cmd-45377ebaa2e24524, cmd-a626340df4ec4fb1) are the expected connection drop/timeout during the reboot itself, not failed mutations. The only residue is two small log files left in /tmp (dnf-podman.log, pull.log) visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot — a low-risk, non-destructive leftover with no security or functional impact, not reverted.
